How the rewrites work: I rewrote all 62 history hits, and I also swept for history phrasing the marker pattern misses. That sweep covered "this commit", M9/pre-M9, "originally", "Earlier iterations", "was once", "the bug", "Regression guard for #N", "now that", "until now", and a list of every `#NNN` in comments. Each block keeps its invariant in the present tense. The narrative and the dated evidence are deleted, and an issue the invariant depends on stays as one link. These are 611 (body.rs test), 685 (resolve_launch_opts), 721 (the lease.rs module and secondary_verdict, where I used an inline link so residency/mod.rs does not grow), 834 (calls.rs), 849 (the process/core.rs header, following the plan's process_runner.rs worked example), 925 (proxy.rs test), 955 (sweep.rs) and 1037 (disable.rs, unchanged). 568 stays as plain text on the temporary port-mismatch diagnostic in process/core.rs; the tracing call itself is untouched. 1091 stays wherever it already stood. I checked every link target number with `gh api` (issue or PR). No fenced block and no `[..]: path` link definition was removed. No pub item lost its last doc line.

The CLI help text: I changed two doc comments on clap fields and checked them against a built binary.
1. benchmark_commands.rs `apply`, the `--apply` help on `gglib benchmark tune`. The line that said "(`--apply-best` is the old name for the ungated version of this and is kept as an alias.)" now says "(`--apply-best` is an alias.)". `gglib benchmark tune --help` shows the new text.
2. config_commands/mod.rs `setup_fast_downloads`, a `hide = true` flag. The "Superseded by…" doc now says the flag provisions the hf_xet accelerator, that `gglib config fast-downloads enable` is the command to use, and why the hidden flag is kept. `config check-deps --help` does not show it.

I also changed "no longer" to "not" on the struct doc of upstream_args.rs `UpstreamArgs`, a flattened Args struct. Neither `chat --help` nor `question --help` prints that text.

One comment was false at the base and is now fixed: retry/test_server.rs said the modelpipe bodies were copied from "version 0.2.0's refusal.rs, the version gglib-app-services pins". gglib-app-services pins modelpipe 0.7.0. defects.what: A rewritten sentence says something false at this commit: "The benchmark harness resolves the floor before the sweep (`benchmark/{agentic,compare,tune}`), which ADR 0009 records." All three entry points pass the setting through. agentic.rs:97, compare.rs:57 and tune/mod.rs:100 each do `settings.as_ref().and_then(|s| s.default_context_size)` with no `.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_CONTEXT_SIZE)`, and each carries a 'Passed through, not resolved' comment. ADR 0009's 2026-08-28 amendment (docs/adr/0009-fit-the-context-to-the-machine.md:258-270) says 'All three now pass the setting through', and scripts/check_context_floor.sh (listing #934) keeps the construct out. The base sentence ('still resolves … rather than fixed here') was already stale. The rewrite restated it in the present tense and dropped the 'still', so the error survives in the form the diet is meant to make trustworthy. This is the author's known failure mode: a repair that brings in a false sentence.
defects.fix: Replace the last two sentences of the first paragraph ('`up` and `serve` pass the setting through too. The benchmark harness resolves the floor before the sweep (`benchmark/{agentic,compare,tune}`), which ADR 0009 records.') with one true sentence, for example: '`up`, `serve` and the benchmark harness (`benchmark/{agentic,compare,tune}`) pass the setting through too, and `scripts/check_context_floor.sh` keeps the resolved floor out of them.' Or delete the benchmark clause outright.

defects.what: The rewrite widened the claim until it is false. The base said 'What is left [of the old unified LlamaError] is the one place that wants a typed error', which was scoped to this type. The new text is 'The orchestration modules in this directory return `anyhow::Result`. This is the one place that wants a *typed* error', which reads as a claim about the whole llama/ directory. That directory also holds server_availability.rs, which defines `LlamaServerError` (thiserror) and `LlamaServerResult<T>`, and command.rs:70 returns `Result<PathBuf, LlamaServerError>`. So 'the one place that wants a typed error' is untrue at this commit.
defects.fix: Scope the claim to this type again, for example: '`LlamaError` exists for one caller that wants a *typed* error: [`InstallPrompt`] is a trait, and a trait in a library should not make its implementors depend on `anyhow`. The install, build, download and update orchestration here returns `anyhow::Result`.' Do not claim uniqueness across the directory, or name `server_availability.rs`'s `LlamaServerError` as the other typed error.

defects.what: The CLI help lost user-facing information. `gglib benchmark tune --help` now ends with '(`--apply-best` is an alias.)'. At the base it said `--apply-best` was the old name for the ungated version and is kept as an alias. `alias` (not `visible_alias`) is hidden, so this sentence is the only place a user learns what `--apply-best` does now. A user whose scripts pass `--apply-best` expecting an ungated apply is no longer told that it now goes through the gate. The orchestrator's rule is that CLI help must not lose information. The history can go, but the behaviour it warned about has to stay, in the present tense.
defects.fix: Change the parenthesis to a present-tense statement that keeps the behaviour, for example: '(`--apply-best` is an alias and goes through the same gate; there is no ungated apply.)' Then rebuild and confirm the text in `gglib benchmark tune --help`.

defects.what: This commit added the sentence "A flag parsed with `.ok()` would serve 4096 here and say nothing." It is false at d661385f. The test calls resolve_default_context(Some("8k"), &Settings::default()). If "8k" were parsed with .ok(), the function would return settings.default_context_size, which is None for Settings::default() (nothing_configured_sends_nothing asserts that). The daemon would then size the context itself: fitted to the machine where it can read the device, and the built-in floor only where it cannot. So the sentence describes the old resolve-to-4096 behaviour. The base text said so: its function doc (base line 28-30) reads "with the pass-through above it would have served something else again, just a different something". The same error was in b48a564e and round 1 did not catch it. It matters because a test doc that names the wrong failure misleads whoever next decides whether the test still guards anything.
